key_insight: Turing Agent orchestrates end-to-end formal verification of research mathematics, turning AI-generated proofs into machine-checked knowledge.
engineering_relevance: A two-scale agent architecture offers a practical approach to coordinating theorem translation, proof construction, and verification across complex mathematical dependencies.
method: Decompose proofs into auxiliary claims and verify them in parallel.
Reuse accumulated proof experience and selectively review semantic fidelity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports approximately 57–62% faithful formalization success on Formal TCS Bench, 83% overall pass@1 on a TCS-focused RLMEval subset, and verification of three previously unresolved TCS tasks.
watch_item: Machine-checked proofs still require semantic scrutiny to ensure the formal statement faithfully represents the intended mathematics; evaluation focuses on theoretical computer science.
paper_title: Turing Agent: Agentic Formal Verification for Mathematical Research
